_note: REAL STATE (no forecast exists on 13 Oct 2026) and EXAMPLE states with made-up numbers, in the dashboard's proposed forecast-contest contract (notes.md). Not published by the F&O tool yet. Research and paper only.

questions.plain: Will NIFTY close higher in 20 trading days (about a month) than today?
questions.yes_when: NIFTY’s close 20 trading days later is above today’s close.

questions.plain: Will NIFTY move 3% or more, up or down, in 20 trading days?
questions.yes_when: NIFTY’s close 20 trading days later is at least 3% away from today’s, either way.

questions.plain: Will NIFTY swing more in the next 20 trading days than in the last 20?
questions.yes_when: NIFTY’s day-to-day swings over the next 20 trading days are bigger than over the last 20.

questions.plain: Will India VIX, the market’s fear gauge, be higher in 10 trading days than today?
questions.yes_when: India VIX’s close 10 trading days later is above today’s close.

questions.plain: Will NIFTY swing less in the next 20 trading days than option prices expect today?
questions.yes_when: NIFTY’s swings over the next 20 trading days are smaller than the swing today’s 30-day option prices imply.

yardsticks.name: What option prices say
yardsticks.plain: The chance hidden in today’s NIFTY option prices. Option prices include a premium for risk, so this is the market’s price, not a true real-world chance.
yardsticks.label: risk-neutral

yardsticks.name: How often it happened
yardsticks.plain: The share of the last 750 trading days (about 3 years) on which the answer was yes.

yardsticks.name: A simple formula
yardsticks.plain: A small textbook formula on recent swings (or on the fear gauge), refitted once a month.

rules.review: the first scheduled review, after 6 months of the three families paper trading together

standing: Profit decides which family trades. Forecast scores only show who reads the market best; a family never gets to trade because it forecasts well.

real.reason: No forecast exists yet, so none can be scored. The contest’s rules wait for an outside review before they are frozen; the yardsticks and Rule-based’s daily forecasts are built after that.

steps.what: The contest’s rules are written and frozen
steps.detail: Draft written; waiting for the outside review, then frozen so no rule can change after a score exists.

steps.what: Rule-based makes its five forecasts every trading day
steps.detail: Starts with G2. Each forecast is saved before 15:00 IST and can never be changed.

steps.what: Each forecast is scored when its answer is known
steps.detail: 10 trading days later for the fear-gauge question, 20 for the other four.

steps.what: Hybrid and AI team join the contest
steps.detail: Comes with their own daily sessions (story F1); until then they show as not running, never as zero.
